newsitem.title: UK: UK's Baldry says most of EU for ending beef ban.
newsitem.headline: UK's Baldry says most of EU for ending beef ban.

text.p: Of all the EU member states, only Germany is opposed to a quick end to the ban on exports of UK beef, according to junior farm minister Tony Baldry.
"With the exception of Germany, most of our European colleagues are keen to get the ban lifted, Baldry told the National Farmers Union annual general meeting on Tuesday.

The EU imposed a ban on all UK exports of beef, beef products and live cattle following the March 20 announcement by health secretary Stephen Dorrell that a new strain of Creutzfeld Jakob's disease had been identified and the conclusion by government scientists that it could be linked to exposure to BSE.

NFU president David Naish attacked the ban as unjustified. And Labour agriculture spokesman Gavin Strang described the furore which followed Dorrell's announcement as "the biggest crisis to hit the industry this century."

Baldry defended the safety record of British beef. "I strongly argue always the pre-eminence of British beef," he said. But there was nothing to be gained from suggesting that beef from other origins was less than safe.
In Germany they had tried to argue that British beef was less safe than the domestic product and the effect was to hit beef consumption generally, he said.
"It's deeply frustrating that we are prevented from gaining access to overseas markets," Baldry said.
